evidence: Accepted the exact finite inverse-power domain clarification after reading the isolated packet and independently checking the primary source at https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3. Section 3 assumes a C2 Euclidean objective. Theorem 3.4 prints h<=1/beta and the inverse-power rate, and separately interprets alpha=0 by its convex limiting coefficient. Lemma 3.5 requires A>0; the subsequent proof sets A=1-alpha*h. Equation (3.3) explicitly permits arbitrary comparators for the one-step inequality. The repair preserves the displayed source optimization setting and labels singular strata separately. It neither silently upgrades the source to the supplied C1 Hilbert theorem nor claims that a limit theorem has been formalized.

findings.detail: Within the nonnegative-curvature contraction regime, alpha>0, h>0, N>=1 and alpha*h<1 give q=1-alpha*h in (0,1), q^N>0, and q^(-N)-1>0. Hence the finite inverse-power expression is well-defined and equals alpha*q^N*R^2/(2*(1-q^N)). N=0 and q=1 make its denominator zero; q=0 makes the negative power undefined in ordinary real arithmetic. No additional objective regularity or minimizer requirement is introduced by the repair. Writing both h>0 and alpha*h>0 when alpha>0 is redundant syntax, not a further restriction. Positive h is stronger than the separate nonnegative-step correction precisely because this normalization divides by a quantity that vanishes at h=0.

Independently compute f(x)=x^2/2, gradient f(x)=x, alpha=beta=h=N=1, x0=1, z=0. Then x1=0 and the actual gap is 0. Lean-totalized 0^(-1)=0 gives coefficient 1/(2*(0-1))=-1/2, so the naive totalized claim would assert 0<=-1/2. This refutes that endpoint reading, not the source formula on its positive domain.

For the same unit quadratic with h=0 and N=1, xN=1 and the gap is 1/2 while q=1 gives totalized coefficient 0. With h=1/2 and N=0, xN=1 and the gap is again 1/2 while q^0=1 gives coefficient 0. Each isolates a genuinely excluded singular parameter stratum.

At alpha*h=1 and N>=1, q=0, so q^N=0 and 1-q^N=1. The rational coefficient is exactly 0 with an ordinary nonzero denominator. The one-step energy inequality with q=0 and h>0 implies f(x1)-f(z)<=0 after dropping its nonnegative squared-distance term, and the same holds at every positive iterate. This directly justifies the endpoint without invoking the positive-A inverse-power recurrence. For a minimizer comparator the gap is therefore exactly zero.

At alpha=0, direct normalization of the weighted estimate yields 2*h*N*(f(xN)-f(z))<=R^2, hence R^2/(2*h*N) when h>0 and N>=1. The strong rational expression instead becomes 0/0, so the convex formula must remain separate. Agreement with the source coefficient is not proof of an analytic alpha-to-zero limiting statement.

Acceptance concerns only the exact repair. The source C2 Euclidean smoothness assumptions, actual constant-step gradient descent, and supplied minimizer in the displayed rate are retained. C1 complete Hilbert objectives, the explicit global upper model, and arbitrary-comparator final rates are distinct theorem generalizations in the candidate packet and remain separate semantic obligations. The zero-base rational extension is clearly distinguished from a direct evaluation of the printed inverse-power formula.
